title: اختبار تدريبي على اختبار شهر نوفمبر - Science - الصف الثاني الإعدادي لغات
scope: November monthly test practice (29/11): from Methods of Heat Transfer to the Chemical Equation.
source: Scope from the science (languages) supervisor, 2026-11-19. All questions from the Performances and Assessments book 2026/2027, Prep 2, Term 1: pp. 23-38.

questions.text: The state in which two objects in contact reach the same temperature, so heat stops flowing between them.
questions.explanation: Heat flows from the hotter object to the colder one until their temperatures are equal: thermal equilibrium (p. 24-26).

questions.text: The energy that transfers from one system to another because of the difference in their temperatures.
questions.explanation: Heat is energy in transfer; temperature measures how hot a system is (p. 26).

questions.text: The transfer of heat through solids from one point to another without the particles moving from their places.
questions.explanation: In conduction, vibrating particles pass energy to neighbouring particles without leaving their places (p. 26).

questions.text: Materials that do not allow heat to pass through them easily, such as wood and plastic.
questions.explanation: Thermal insulators have low thermal conductivity; metals such as silver and copper are good thermal conductors (p. 26).

questions.text: Substances that increase the speed of a chemical reaction without being consumed or changed.
questions.explanation: A catalyst is written on the arrow of the equation as (cat) (p. 33).

questions.text: The total mass of the reactants in a chemical reaction equals the total mass of the products.
questions.explanation: Matter is neither created nor destroyed in a reaction; the atoms are only rearranged (p. 33).

questions.text: A change in which new substances with new properties are formed.
questions.explanation: Burning wood is a chemical change; melting ice is a physical change because no new substance forms (p. 29 and 38).

questions.text: Numbers written below and to the right of the symbols in a chemical formula to show the number of atoms.
questions.explanation: In H₂O the subscript 2 shows two hydrogen atoms. Coefficients are the numbers written before formulas to balance equations (p. 33).

questions.text: Heat transfers in three different ways: ......
questions.explanation: Heat moves by conduction (mainly in solids), convection (liquids and gases) and radiation (no medium needed) (p. 27).

questions.text: Energy transfers from a system with a ...... temperature to a system with a ...... temperature.
questions.explanation: Heat always flows from the hotter system to the colder one (p. 27).

questions.text: A thermal camera detects the ...... radiation emitted by objects and converts it into coloured images.
questions.explanation: Warm bodies emit infrared radiation, which thermal cameras turn into images (p. 27).

questions.text: In a chemical equation, the symbol (aq) means ......
choices: aqueous solution (a substance dissolved in water)
questions.explanation: (s) solid or precipitate, (l) liquid, (g) gas, (v) vapour, (aq) aqueous solution (p. 33).

questions.text: The symbol Δ written on the arrow of a chemical equation means ......
questions.explanation: Δ heat, cat catalyst, dil dilute acid, conc concentrated acid (p. 33).

questions.text: The chemical formula of copper sulphate is ......
questions.explanation: Copper sulphate is CuSO₄; zinc sulphate is ZnSO₄ (p. 31).

questions.text: The balanced equation for the electrolysis of water is ......
questions.explanation: There are 4 H and 2 O atoms on each side only in 2H₂O → 2H₂ + O₂ (p. 32).

questions.text: The balanced equation for burning aluminum in oxygen is ......
questions.explanation: 4 Al and 6 O atoms on each side: 4Al + 3O₂ → 2Al₂O₃ (p. 34).

questions.text: Firefighters wear shiny silver suits, because ......
choices: shiny surfaces reflect heat radiation, so they absorb less heat
silver is a good thermal conductor
questions.explanation: Dark, dull surfaces absorb radiation; shiny surfaces reflect it (p. 26).

questions.text: Cooking utensils are made of metal, while their handles are made of wood or plastic, because ......
choices: metals are thermal insulators, while wood and plastic are conductors
wood and plastic are cheaper than metal
metals do not transfer heat by conduction
metals are good thermal conductors, while wood and plastic are thermal insulators
questions.explanation: The metal pot heats the food quickly, and the insulating handle does not burn the hand (p. 27).

questions.text: Polystyrene panels are used between hollow bricks when building walls, because ......
choices: polystyrene is a thermal insulator that reduces heat transfer
polystyrene is a good thermal conductor
questions.explanation: It keeps buildings cool in summer and warm in winter (p. 26-27).

questions.text: The electric heater is placed on the floor of the room, because ......
choices: hot air sinks to the floor
the floor reflects the heat radiation
hot air rises and cold air sinks, forming convection currents that heat the whole room
questions.explanation: Heated air expands, becomes less dense and rises; cooler, denser air sinks to replace it (p. 27).

questions.text: The freezer is placed at the top of the refrigerator, because ......
choices: cold air rises to the top
the top is closer to the motor
cold air is denser and sinks, cooling the parts below by convection
questions.explanation: The same convection currents that rise from a heater sink from a freezer (p. 27).

questions.text: The sea breeze occurs during the day, because ......
choices: heat moves from the sea to the land by conduction
land heats faster than sea water, so the hot air over the land rises and cooler air from the sea replaces it
the air over the sea is hotter
sea water heats faster than land
questions.explanation: Land has a lower specific heat than water, so its temperature rises faster (p. 26-27).

questions.text: Heat transfers from the Sun to the Earth despite the great empty distance between them, because ......
choices: conduction can happen in a vacuum
radiation does not need a medium to travel through
convection can happen in a vacuum
questions.explanation: Conduction and convection need particles of matter; radiation travels as electromagnetic waves through a vacuum (p. 26-27).

questions.text: Snakes are able to hunt their prey at night, because ......
choices: they sense the infrared radiation emitted by the bodies of their prey
their prey glows in the dark
they see well in visible light
they feel the prey by conduction
questions.explanation: Warm bodies give off infrared radiation even in the dark (p. 27).

questions.text: When a zinc plate is placed in blue copper sulphate solution, the blue colour disappears, because ......
choices: zinc replaces copper, forming colourless zinc sulphate, and copper is deposited
questions.explanation: Zn + CuSO₄ → ZnSO₄ + Cu: a chemical reaction shown by a colour change (p. 31).

questions.text: The melting of a candle is a physical change, while the burning of coal is a chemical change, because ......
choices: melting forms no new substance, while burning forms new substances
melting forms new substances, while burning does not
questions.explanation: A chemical change produces new substances with new properties (p. 31).

questions.text: What happens when silver nitrate solution is added to sodium chloride solution?
choices: A white precipitate of silver chloride forms
questions.explanation: AgNO₃(aq) + NaCl(aq) → AgCl(s) + NaNO₃(aq); silver chloride does not dissolve in water (p. 29).

questions.text: What happens when a magnesium strip is placed in a test tube of dilute hydrochloric acid?
choices: Copper is deposited on the strip
questions.explanation: Mg(s) + 2HCl(aq) → MgCl₂(aq) + H₂(g) (p. 29).

questions.text: What happens when a magnesium ribbon is lit in air?
choices: It burns with a dazzling light and heat, forming a white powder of magnesium oxide
questions.explanation: 2Mg(s) + O₂(g) → 2MgO(s). Hold it with tongs and protect your eyes (p. 29 and 38).

questions.text: What happens when sodium hydroxide (caustic soda) is heated with cooking oil and stirred continuously?
choices: A white precipitate of silver chloride forms
Soap forms, and the texture of the mixture changes
questions.explanation: This chemical reaction is how soap is made (p. 29 and 31).

questions.text: Two identical copper cubes at 70°C and 50°C touch each other. What happens?
choices: Heat flows from the 70°C cube to the 50°C cube until both reach about 60°C
Heat flows from the 50°C cube to the 70°C cube
questions.explanation: Heat flows from hot to cold until thermal equilibrium; identical cubes meet halfway (p. 24).

questions.text: Heat cannot transfer through a vacuum by conduction or convection.
questions.explanation: True. Both need particles of matter; only radiation travels through a vacuum (p. 26).

questions.text: The pipes of solar heaters are painted black because black surfaces reflect heat radiation.
questions.explanation: False. Black surfaces absorb heat radiation best, so the water in the pipes heats up faster (p. 25).

questions.text: The melting of ice is a chemical change.
questions.explanation: False. It is a physical change: no new substance forms (p. 38).

questions.text: A chemical equation is balanced when the number of atoms of each element in the reactants equals their number in the products.
questions.explanation: True. A balanced equation obeys the law of conservation of mass (p. 33).

questions.text: Unlike convection, radiation ......
choices: can transfer heat through a vacuum without a medium
happens only in liquids and gases
questions.explanation: Convection moves heat with moving particles of liquids and gases; radiation is electromagnetic waves (p. 27).

questions.text: Which pair gives a thermal conductor and then a thermal insulator?
questions.explanation: Silver and copper conduct heat well; wood, plastic and polystyrene are insulators (p. 27 and 37).

questions.text: How can you infer that a chemical reaction happens when you fry an egg?
choices: The colour and texture of the egg change, and they do not change back
The egg's mass decreases by half
questions.explanation: A lasting change in colour and state is a sign of a chemical reaction (p. 31).

questions.text: How can you infer that a chemical reaction happens when you light fireworks?
choices: Light, heat and colours are given off
questions.explanation: Emission of light and heat is one of the signs of a chemical reaction (p. 29 and 31).

questions.text: How can you infer that a chemical reaction happens when you add a magnesium strip to dilute hydrochloric acid?
questions.explanation: Evolution of a gas is a sign of a chemical reaction (p. 31).
